Where'd my acorns go?

lines.text: Your bank is required to keep 0% of your deposit.
lines.say: Your bank is required to keep zero percent of your deposit.

lines.text: Squirrel deposits 100 acorns. The bank doesn't lock them all up.
lines.say: Squirrel deposits a hundred acorns. The bank doesn't lock them all up.

lines.text: Our math: the bank keeps 10 acorns and lends 90 to a chipmunk.
lines.say: Our math: the bank keeps ten acorns and lends ninety to a chipmunk.

lines.text: That's fractional reserve banking. Keep a slice, lend the rest.
lines.say: That's fractional reserve banking. Keep a slice, lend the rest.

lines.text: The slice sits as vault cash or as reserves at the Federal Reserve.
lines.say: The slice sits as vault cash, or as reserves at the Federal Reserve.

lines.text: Since March 26, 2020, the Fed's required slice has been 0%.
lines.say: Since March twenty-sixth, twenty twenty, the Fed's required slice has been zero percent.

lines.text: Yet banks still kept about $3.2 trillion at the Fed in 2025, on average.
lines.say: Yet banks still kept about three point two trillion dollars at the Fed in twenty twenty-five, on average.

lines.text: Twist: the Bank of England said in 2014 that new loans create new deposits.
lines.say: Twist: the Bank of England said in twenty fourteen that new loans create new deposits.

lines.text: If a bank fails, FDIC covers up to $250,000 per depositor, per bank, per ownership category.
lines.say: If a bank fails, F D I C covers up to two hundred fifty thousand dollars per depositor, per bank, per ownership category.

post.title: Why your bank doesn't keep your deposit in a vault
post.ig:
Your bank is required to keep 0% of your deposit in reserve.

The Fed cut reserve requirements to 0% effective March 26, 2020.
Banks still held about $3.2 trillion at the Fed on average in 2025 (FRED, reserve balances).
Our math: deposit 100 acorns, the bank keeps 10 and lends 90. The Bank of England (2014) notes that new loans create new deposits.
FDIC covers up to $250,000 per depositor, per insured bank, per ownership category.

Sources: Federal Reserve; FRED (WRESBAL); Bank of England Quarterly Bulletin 2014 Q1; FDIC; example math by FinancePros TV.
News and education, not financial advice.

post.yt_desc:
Fractional reserve banking means a bank keeps a slice of deposits as vault cash or reserves at the Fed and lends the rest (example math: deposit 100 acorns, keep 10, lend 90). The Fed cut reserve requirements to 0% effective March 26, 2020, yet banks held about $3.2 trillion at the Fed on average in 2025 (FRED WRESBAL), and FDIC covers up to $250,000 per depositor, per insured bank, per ownership category. The Bank of England (2014) explains that new loans create new deposits. News and education, not financial advice.
